fichas.title: Cemetery layout and graves
fichas.summary: Cemetery planning guidance covers facilities, groundwater and water supply, path and planting layouts, grave types, grave-marker proportions, grave depths, and indicative grave sizes and periods of use. Earth burials are placed along main paths, boundary walls, and path ends; urn burials are placed in planting belts, urn groves, and hedge fences.

CEMETERIES
Graves, Cemetery Chapel

Overall cemetery facilities

Assembly area for mourners, stands for sale of wreaths and
flowers, WCs. Groundwater table £2.50-3.00 m deep, which
may require drainage. A large water supply pipe is necessary for
watering.
The best exploitation of space is achieved by straight paths
and the division of the cemetery into groups with similar grave
sizes, like urns, purchased, children's and adults' graves ---+ 0.
Dimensions of the group areas: 30 x 30-40 x 40 m.
Planting with trees and shrubs is often an essential design feature,
and some possibilities are tree strips within the cemetery, larger
stands of trees as a boundary or outside the plot, high hedges or
groups of shrubs to offer orientation.
Graves and gravestones

e

C) Double graves

gravestones, the size (see following table) and colour mostly
uniform.

sizes, like urns, purchased, children's and adults' graves ---+ 0.

and some possibilities are tree strips within the cemetery, larger
stands of trees as a boundary or outside the plot, high hedges or
groups of shrubs to offer orientation.

fichas.title: Columbarium and crematorium chapel
fichas.summary: A columbarium stores urns not intended for burial, as either a room or a wall with niches. The crematorium chapel serves all denominations and is placed according to cemetery size and layout. Its form affects the funeral ceremony; the functional diagram shows the chapel alongside ancillary rooms.
